assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turned the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery into a programmable chemical tool: bifunctional degraders and molecular glues convert a biological process into a defined, designable chemical reaction (induced proximity). Original concept, broad generality across targets, and already clinical-stage, which gives unusual impact for both chemistry and medicine.
assessment.attribution: PROTAC concept and first proof are credited to Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto); Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins the molecular-glue branch. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later advances, so credit is crowded; a three-person split of concept plus mechanism is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed by many independent groups (structures of ternary complexes, degradation kinetics), and clinical trials are ongoing. Late-stage clinical approval is still pending, so timing may be slightly early but the chemistry is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the PROTAC invention or on molecular glues/cereblon biology
Clinical efficacy not yet established by approved drugs
Crowded credit among many strong contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs lets chemists install non-natural amino acids site-specifically in living cells. A clean, original chemical solution to a biological constraint, with lasting impact as a general tool in protein engineering, imaging and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues (including Lei Wang) made the founding demonstrations in E. coli and yeast; Chin extended it to eukaryotes, multiple distinct codons and whole-organism use. Lei Wang's early role is real, so the choice of two laureates leaves a defensible but not perfect attribution.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across hundreds of laboratories for two decades; method stable and routinely used. Recognition is timely or even overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama
I am relying on memory of the priority sequence rather than verification

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing performs a direct chemical conversion of one base to another at a targeted genomic site without a double-strand break, built by pairing engineered deaminase chemistry with a programmable DNA binder. Original and very high impact, and the mechanism is a well-defined enzymatic reaction.
assessment.attribution: Liu led both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on the respective papers and the adenine editor required extensive directed evolution. Liu alone is the most natural laureate; adding Komor or Gaudelli is possible but unusual. Nishida/Kondo's parallel cytidine deaminase work is a priority question I would want clarified.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication, multiple therapeutic programmes and early clinical results. Recognition could be timely, though the field is young and long-term safety (off-target deamination, bystander edits) is still being characterised.
uncertainties: Priority overlap with the Nishida/Kondo cytidine editor
Overlap with the CRISPR prize in 2020 might make the committee cautious

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics made it possible to measure thousands of proteins and their modifications in a cell, replacing assumptions with measurements. An enabling tool of broad importance, with methods (shotgun/MudPIT, SILAC, SRM/SWATH) that became standard.
assessment.attribution: The field has many distinct methodological contributions and three clear leaders fit: Mann for high-resolution quantitative and phosphoproteomics, Aebersold for targeted and systems proteomics, Yates for shotgun/MudPIT. Hunt, Gygi and Heck also have credible claims, so any trio omits strong people.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature, reproduced everywhere and still advancing; recognition is not premature, though the Nobel in 2002 for MS of biomolecules covers part of the foundation.
uncertainties: Overlap with 2002 prize on ionisation methods
Which of several parallel technical advances should carry the credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Determining the structure of the nitrogenase iron-molybdenum cofactor, including its interstitial carbide, and the catalytic cycle of N2 reduction addresses a long-standing fundamental chemical problem with enormous biological and agricultural relevance.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle produced the key crystallographic advances on FeMo-cofactor; Seefeldt and Dean contributed enzymology and mechanism, and Ribbe the biosynthesis. Credit is shared across structure and mechanism and there is a risk of a messy split.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed independently and at high resolution, but the true mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is still debated, so interpretation is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction still unresolved
Allocation between structural and mechanistic contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made routine, automated chemical synthesis of DNA possible and underlies primers, probes, sequencing libraries, synthetic genes and oligonucleotide drugs. An archetype of a chemical invention that became infrastructure for biology.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers is the central inventor of the phosphoramidite method; Hood's contribution is mainly instrument automation. Caruthers alone is a clean attribution, though earlier phosphotriester and phosphite work by Khorana, Letsinger and others affects the narrative.
assessment.maturity: Completely mature and universally validated; the only issue is that recognition is long delayed, with risk that the main figures are advanced in age.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views it as dated rather than current

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules electrically through nanopores converts a chemical identity into a measurable current and allows long-read sequencing and direct RNA modification detection. A clear, original concept that was developed into a widely used technology.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton proposed and demonstrated nucleotide passage, Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled translocation; Kasianowicz showed polymer detection. Credit is plausibly three people but Branton and Kasianowicz would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Commercial and academic validation is strong, with accuracy improving; the field is mature enough but still evolving, so slightly early compared with others on my list.
uncertainties: Historic priority between Branton/Deamer and Kasianowicz
Whether this is a chemistry or a physics/technology prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemical delivery solution that made siRNA and mRNA medicines practical, and were decisive for the COVID-19 vaccines. Impact is clear and large, though the underlying chemistry is an optimisation of lipid structure and formulation rather than a single mechanistic discovery.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed across multiple groups and companies (Cullis, Hope, MacLachlan, Madden for ionizable lipid formulation; Anderson and Langer for combinatorial lipid libraries), with patent disputes. A fair three-laureate configuration is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Large-scale clinical validation exists; the science is mature and recognition is timely after the 2023 Medicine prize, but attribution and the novelty of the chemistry remain debated.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as pharmaceutical formulation rather than fundamental chemistry
Medicine prize 2023 already honoured the mRNA side
